blocks.text: Administrators can define and set up policy rules for device usage based on criteria, severity, action, etc. Additionally, they can create a single rule to manage multiple removable storage devices, associating them with specific users or endpoints (Device Per User) by either manually adding devices or importing a CSV file which has device data. The administrator can perform the following operations:

blocks.item: Add a Removable Storage Rule
Go to Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Device Control > Removable Storage.
Click Add Rule and choose one of the following:
Removable Storage
Device Per User
The New Exception page opens. Specify settings in the rule editor for the removable storage device per user.
Details: Configure the following details:
Rule Name: Enter a rule name for the device control policy.
Description: Enter additional notes or information about the rule. The description cannot exceed 250 characters.

Rule Status: Select to enable the rule. An enabled rule is actively enforced. A disabled rule is not actively enforced but does not lose its place in the rule order. The service skips it and moves to the next rule.
Severity: Select the severity of the violation from the drop-down menu (i.e., High, Medium, Low, or Info).

Rule Order: Select the rule order from the drop-down menu. Policy rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order (Rule 1 before Rule 2, and so on), and the rule order reflects this rule's place in the order. Rule evaluation stops at the first match.
Action: Select an action (i.e., Allow, Block, Read Only, or None) for violation that matches the criteria in the rule.
End User Notification: Select whether to Show or Hide a notification about the violation on the endpoint.
Criteria:
Click Add.
Choose one of the following options:

Import Devices: Select Import Device. The Import window appears where you can drag and drop files or click to browse. You can upload a CSV file up to 50 MB. You can also download a sample file and modify it as per your requirement.
See image.

You can import CSV files that contain removable storage serial numbers that are linked to an authorized Zscaler Client Connector user's email address in the rule editor. Each CSV row creates a rule criterion. When subsequent CSV files are imported under the same rule, new rows are appended to the criteria. Existing criteria are not updated, duplicated, or deleted.
Add Devices: You can manually add devices by entering the following information:
Serial Number: Enter the removable storage device's serial number. The default value is Any.
VID: Enter the Vendor ID of the removable storage device. The default value is Any.
PID: Enter the removable storage device's product ID number. The default value is Any.
Endpoint: Enter the name of the endpoints connected to the user's device. The default value is Any.
User: Enter the email address of the Zscaler Client Connector user. The default value is Any.
Description: Enter additional notes or information about the rule.
Click Save.
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.
Edit a Removable Storage Rule
Go to Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Device Control > Removable Storage.
Locate the removable storage rule or the removable storage device per user rule (identified by the device user pairs in the Criteria column) in the list, then click the Edit icon.
The Edit Exception page opens depending on the rule you selected.
Edit the settings for the selected rule as required.
See Image.
Click Save and activate the change.
You can delete any rule by selecting the rule from the list and clicking the Delete icon.
You can edit the default removable storage rule, but you cannot delete it.
The New Exception page opens. Specify settings in the rule editor for the removable storage device.
Details: Configure the following details:
Rule Name: Enter a rule name for the device control policy.
Description: Enter additional notes or information about the rule. The description cannot exceed 250 characters.

Rule Status: Select to enable the rule. An enabled rule is actively enforced. A disabled rule is not actively enforced but does not lose its place in the rule order. The service skips it and moves to the next rule.
Severity: Select the severity of the violation from the drop-down menu (i.e., High, Medium, Low, or Info).

Rule Order: Select the rule order from the drop-down menu. Policy rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order (Rule 1 before Rule 2, and so on), and the rule order reflects this rule's place in the order. Rule evaluation stops at the first match.
Action: Select an action (i.e., Allow, Block, Read Only, or None) for violation that matches the criteria in the rule.
End User Notification: Select whether to Show or Hide a notification about the violation on the endpoint.

Criteria: Select one or all of the following options. If not selected, the service ignores the criterion. The rule triggers based on the following relationships: [Removable Storage AND (Users OR User Groups OR Departments) AND (Device OR Device Group) AND Network Type AND Device Trust Level AND User Risk Profile].

Removable Storage: Select All Removable Storage Devices to apply the rule to all removable storage devices, or select one or more removable storage devices from the drop-down list under Inventory. You can search for a removable storage device. Click Resources to select a removable storage device from existing resources or add a removable storage device.
Users: Select one or more users to apply the rule to those users. You can also search for users.
User Groups: Select one or more user groups to apply the rule to those user groups. You can also search for user groups.
Departments: Select one or more departments to apply the rule to those departments. You can also search for departments.
Device: Select one or more devices to apply the rule to those devices. You can also search for devices.

Network Type: Select one or more network types to apply the rule to those network types (i.e., Trusted, Off-Trusted, or VPN). Ensure endpoints are running the following Zscaler Client Connector versions for rule enforcement:
Windows: 4.8.600 or later
macOS: 4.7.1 or later
Device Group: Select one or more device groups to apply the rule to those device groups. You can also search for device groups.
Device Trust Level: Select the device trust level values (i.e., High, Medium, Low, or Unknown) to which the rule applies.
User Risk Profile: Select the user risk score levels to which the rule applies. A range of risk scores is grouped as a risk score level. The following user risk score levels are available:
Low: User risk scores ranging from 0 to 29.
Medium: User risk scores ranging from 30 to 59.
High: User risk scores ranging from 60 to 79.
Critical: User risk scores ranging from 80 to 100.
See Image.
Click Save and activate the change.
Delete a Removable Storage Rule

blocks.text: After the policy rules are set, they need to be activated for them to be enforced. To learn more, see Activating Device Control Policy Rules, Configuration, and Indexed Documents Changes.
